speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To begin my assessment, on which side of your neck does the pain originate, and which specific fingers are affected by the numbness or tingling?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your age, diabetes, and the progressive nature of your symptoms affecting both hands, could you describe whether the pain radiates specifically into the thumb/index finger or the middle/ring/little fingers? Additionally, have you noticed any clumsiness with buttons or difficulty holding objects?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with possible cervical spondylotic myelopathy.
